 "content": "# Continual-ARC pattern: bridge gaps between aligned diamond motifs

Observed and verified on task-4882da25. Each motif is a four-cell diamond (2 at top/bottom tips and two lateral points on the middle row). When two diamonds face each other along the same row, fill the intervening cells with 1 between their facing lateral points. When aligned vertically, fill the gap with 1 between the facing tips. Preserve every 2 and all other cells; bridge only where motif pairs are actually aligned.

Demo evidence:
- Demo 1: same-row diamonds at row 1, with their facing sides at columns 4 and 9; output inserts 1 in columns 5–8.
- Demo 2: three diamonds across row 3; output bridges the two facing gaps (1s), and the center diamond has vertical 1-bridges in rows 5–7 connecting to a diamond below at the same column. A separate lower horizontal pair is bridged likewise.
- Demo 3: two horizontal pairs at rows 4 and 9, plus vertically aligned sides at columns 4 and 11; outputs fill each gap with 1.

Test solved: horizontal bridge row 6 between diamonds centered columns 2 and 10; vertical bridge at column 2 between motifs centered rows 2 and 6 (row 4 receives 1). This was the final correct answer. Key: identify diamonds by exact masks and connect aligned neighboring pairs; don't connect merely nearby or misaligned motifs.
